threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' without the London accent. Locals say 'the underground' and avoid eye contact at all costs.
Caught a glimpse of a bloke on the 35 bus, serenading a stray cat under the streetlamp. Only in Brixton would that not even raise an eyebrow.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I stepped onto the U7, packed with kids blasting their playlists and a stray cat lounging on the platform. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can buy a beer and a döner from a kiosk at 3 AM while waiting for the night bus—Berlin’s late-night hustle is unmatched.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they subtly avoid eye contact with the crazy guy singing opera on the corner of 24th and Mission. It's like a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dude in a full suit calmly reading a newspaper while Muni sat dead in the tunnel. Only in SF does the chaos seem so serene.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the local bars close early. But if you wander deep enough, some don’t get busy until after midnight, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them in Gràcia when they ask for 'tap water' at restaurants, still baffled by the 'sin gas' and 'con gas' labels.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'double-decker' instead of just 'the bus' and avoid the numbers like it's some kind of quiz.
Caught the N1 last night, and a guy in a neon parka was arguing with a lamppost. He said it was his ex's fault. Classic South London drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw the wild street party at Hermannplatz - a mix of DJ sets and spontaneous dance-offs among strangers, all under the neon lights.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it’s totally normal to find a full-on techno party in a former factory with no sign outside. Just follow the sound!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the exact taco truck that has the shortest line and the best al pastor at 2 AM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus arguing passionately with the driver about the route. Turns out, he was just trying to get to the nearest taco truck.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the side streets that hold the real charm—tiny bakeries and unmarked bars only locals know.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their overuse of 'de nada' after a simple thank you. In Eixample, locals just nod and move on.
